cohort: The study included 10,620 women with moderate or severe anaemia giving birth vaginally in hospitals across Pakistan, Nigeria, Tanzania, and Zambia.
finding: A 10 g/L reduction in prebirth haemoglobin significantly increased the odds of clinical (aOR 1.29), WHO-defined (aOR 1.25), and calculated (aOR 1.23) postpartum haemorrhage, and severe anaemia was associated with seven times higher odds of death or near miss compared to moderate anaemia.
